subject: A few incorrect results using the defaults for occu

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: A few incorrect results using the defaults for occu
parts:
I have found a few instances where using the defaults for occu (and no covariates) where there is convergence and no indication there is a problem but the results for the maximum likelihood estimates for psi and p (probability of presence and detection probability, respectively) are not close enough to the true maximum likelihood estimates.  I can get occu to obtain close enough estimates by either making the relative tolerance parameter (reltol) very small or putting in starting values other than the defaults (which appear to me to be zero).

For the example attached I have 30 sites with 3 visits each (no missing values).  occu with the defaults gives estimates of psi-hat = 0.9996363 and p-hat 0.3668276.  By changing reltol = 1E-15 I get psi-hat = 0.8660276 and p-hat 0.4233891.  By added in "starts=c(0.1,0.1)" I get psi-hat = 0.8660271 and p-hat 0.4233893.  (The latter two sets are essentially the correct values.) 

My question is what in the output should I have noticed that would have told me I had the wrong result?  I've looked at "str" of the output object but I don't what to look at to know I should have changed the defaults.

I appreciate any guidance.

Thanks,

Jim

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] A few incorrect results using the defaults for occu
parts:
hi Jim,
 This is an interesting as it seems to be an outright failure of optim() for a very simple data set.  Worse, the convergence code (if you look at the summary(output) ) says "0" which means convergence was achieved so maybe it looks good at first glance.
 The only thing I see that is suspect is the NaN for the standard errors resulting from the boundary estimate which might prompt one to dig a little deeper.

 I'm not sure what the best approach would be to dealing with this. Maybe we need some specific warning in the summary output but its not clear to me that catching NaN standard errors would solve the problem. I'm curious what other thoughts are on this and whether other people have observed these kinds of failures.

regards
andy

On Mon, Aug 18, 2014 at 4:39 PM, Jim Baldwin, USDA Forest Service <jbald...@gmail.com> wrote:
I have found a few instances where using the defaults for occu (and no covariates) where there is convergence and no indication there is a problem but the results for the maximum likelihood estimates for psi and p (probability of presence and detection probability, respectively) are not close enough to the true maximum likelihood estimates.  I can get occu to obtain close enough estimates by either making the relative tolerance parameter (reltol) very small or putting in starting values other than the defaults (which appear to me to be zero).

For the example attached I have 30 sites with 3 visits each (no missing values).  occu with the defaults gives estimates of psi-hat = 0.9996363 and p-hat 0.3668276.  By changing reltol = 1E-15 I get psi-hat = 0.8660276 and p-hat 0.4233891.  By added in "starts=c(0.1,0.1)" I get psi-hat = 0.8660271 and p-hat 0.4233893.  (The latter two sets are essentially the correct values.) 

My question is what in the output should I have noticed that would have told me I had the wrong result?  I've looked at "str" of the output object but I don't what to look at to know I should have changed the defaults.

I appreciate any guidance.

Thanks,

Jim
